svg.title: Fixed vectors and simple-function coboundaries form a dense pointwise-good core
svg.desc: A blue fixed-vector lane has positive-horizon orbit averages equal to the chosen representative, so the sequence is eventually constant after horizon zero. A clay simple-coboundary lane telescopes because its representative has finite bounded range. The two lanes add to a green fixed-plus-simple-coboundary core. Hilbert projection and density show this core is dense in square-integrable space. Representative transport proves almost-everywhere convergence on the core. A dashed final arrow to every integrable observable is labeled as the missing maximal closure step.
svg.text: Build a dense class where pointwise convergence is already algebraic
Geometry proves density; representative bookkeeping proves almost-everywhere goodness.
FIXED VECTORS
Koopman composition leaves the vector fixed
one conull set works for every natural iterate
positive-horizon averages equal the chosen representative
SIMPLE COBOUNDARIES
generator has a finite-range representative
finite range gives bounded endpoints
telescoping averages converge to zero
FIXED PLUS SIMPLE COBOUNDARY CORE
closed under the one addition needed by the definition
almost-everywhere equal representatives transport convergence events
DENSITY CERTIFICATE
projection plus orthogonal residual
simple generators approximate the residual
POINTWISE-GOOD CERTIFICATE
full averages converge almost everywhere on the core
the limit is not identified for a general core sum
both facts are needed
Missing: a weak-maximal closure argument extending convergence to every integrable observable.
Takeaway: density and pointwise goodness are proved separately; maximal closure is still missing.
